title: Garrett Crochet pitches off Fenway mound at 80 to 90 percent: ‘I just want to contribute’
content:
BOSTON — In a race against time for Garrett Crochet and the Boston Red Sox, the left-hander checked off another box in his effort to return to the team for the postseason: pitching off the mound at Fenway Park.

The 27-year-old threw roughly 25 pitches at an 80 to 90 percent effort in his third bullpen session — his first on the main mound at Fenway with cameras set up to measure his pitch metrics. About 15 teammates, coaches and front-office members watched closely. The lefty mixed in his sweeper for the first time and hit 92.5 mph with his fastball as he slowly adds velocity and intensity in each successive outing. He’s scheduled for another bullpen outing Tuesday in Boston.

With the Triple-A season ending Sept. 20, the calendar is tight for Crochet, who is being brought back as a reliever, to get into a rehab game before the postseason begins. It’s possible he could pitch one or two innings in a simulated game against Red Sox teammates and then enter the playoff fray. Asked how realistic he thought it’d be to pitch in a game before the playoffs, Crochet remained optimistic.

“I’m not sure. Trending well, right now,” he said. “Have a lot more stuff to tick off. This is my first time throwing sweepers in a bullpen, so it’d be a pretty big leap to put myself in a game mindset right now. It’s also like, whatever I say to you guys and (then) I don’t do it, then I look like a dumbass. And I’ve done that a couple of times. So, really, just keep trending, keep doing what the team and the staff asked me to do.”

Crochet threw his first bullpen a week ago and his second on Tuesday, a schedule of every three or four days. With the idea he’ll contribute out of the bullpen for one or two innings, his mound sessions likely won’t exceed 30 pitches. Crochet is focused on getting back as quickly as possible.

“Watching what this team has done all year long, kind of kicking myself because I just want to contribute,” he said. “Last year we felt like we had a good squad, and this year they’re taking another step forward. And I hate that I can’t be a part of it, but it’s been a joy to watch. Really proud of those guys, but at the same time, want to be a part of what they’ve put together.”

Crochet landed on the IL on April 26 with shoulder inflammation and attempted to return a month later, but was shut down after a late-May live batting-practice session against hitters, during which he reaggravated the shoulder. He spent all of June and July shut down from throwing, focusing solely on shoulder strength, and finally began throwing again at 50-60 feet on Aug. 3.

“I feel like I got ahead of myself when I threw that live back in May, and then things obviously took a turn as the injury matured,” he said. “Right now, it’s just taking it step by step.”

Crochet was pleased with his execution on Friday in his highest-intensity throwing session thus far.

“Shoulder feels really good,” he added. “For me, it’s like the rest of my body is getting acclimated to throwing this intense again. Had four months to work on the shoulder, and it’s in a really good spot.”

Interim manager Chad Tracy remained cautious about Crochet’s progress.

“We’re still in ‘check one box at a time’ (phase),” Tracy said. “Not, ‘Oh, he threw off a mound, let’s rush Garrett back.’ Very mindful of what he can bring, and also very mindful of what he means for the future. So as long as we keep taking steps forward, we’re in a good spot. He took another one today, and we’ll see how he does over the course of next week as well.”

The Red Sox also placed outfielder Eli White on the injured list on Friday with a right foot ligament injury after he crashed into the wall Tuesday night. White was still getting imaging on his foot before Friday’s game, but he was in a walking boot and on crutches, indicating he’ll be out for a significant amount of time. Acquired at the trade deadline from Atlanta for pitcher Tyler Uberstine, White had produced well for the Red Sox — especially in the absence of Ceddanne Rafaela, who’s been on the IL with a right quad injury. White had hit .276 with three doubles and a homer in 27 games.

Rafaela, meanwhile, is eligible to return to the team Sunday, but Tracy said he will likely need a few more days.

“I think he’s getting close,” Tracy said. “The biggest thing with Rafa is making sure the strength numbers are in the appropriate spot before they really ramp up sprint exposure. He is running right now, jogging, not high-intent running. (He’s) hitting, throwing, all that’s good. But until that strength number gets where they want it, that’s when they’ll ramp sprint exposure. And once he does that for two, three days, hopefully we’ll have him.”

Infielder Anthony Seigler was recalled to replace White’s spot on the roster. The Red Sox might have recalled outfielder Kristian Campbell, but he landed on the IL in Triple A with a right foot injury Thursday. White had been playing regularly in Rafaela’s absence, but it’s likely now that Roman Anthony will play more in left field rather than designated hitter, and Jarren Duran will shift from left to center field, especially against right-handed starters. Against lefties, Nate Eaton is likely to start in center.

Willson Contreras, who’s been out since Aug. 31 with a hamstring strain, will begin a rehab assignment Friday for Double-A Portland, where he will DH. Contreras is scheduled to play a second rehab game on Saturday at first base. After missing the past 10 days, Contreras told Tracy he wanted to see live pitching and play in the field before returning to the Red Sox. They’ll reevaluate him after Saturday’s game.
